t: A Korean kingdom founded by Wang Geon in 918 that reunited the peninsula in 936 and ruled it from Kaegyong (Kaesong).
Buddhism was the state religion: the court carved the Tripitaka Koreana, and Goryeo potters perfected inlaid celadon.
Military rule from 1170 and Mongol overlordship from 1259 weakened the crown, and Yi Seong-gye replaced it with Joseon in 1392.
dyk: The Jikji, printed at Heungdeoksa temple in Cheongju in 1377, is the oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type; its only surviving volume is in the National Library of France.
ev: Wang Geon is raised to the throne and founds Goryeo
Taejo defeats Later Baekje, completing the reunification of the peninsula
Gang Gam-chan destroys a Khitan army at the Battle of Gwiju
Military officers seize power and depose King Uijong
The court withdraws to Ganghwa Island during the Mongol invasions
Carving of the Tripitaka Koreana woodblocks is completed
Yi Seong-gye deposes King Gongyang and founds Joseon
